To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
observational learning can be understood as the learning of observational prediction errors, which can be observed in brain activity of the dorsolateral and the ventromesial prefrontal cortices.

the brain regions involved in observational learning can be divided into two groups, one that is active when the observed action is different from the expected action, and one that is active in response to a different outcome than the expected outcome.

human observational learning is supported by two previously unexplored forms of prediction error (observational action and outcome prediction errors) and by neural signals in the dorsolaterl and ventromedial parts of the prefrontal cortex.
